search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting Salmonella cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and outbreak details in the United States during May–July 2024, covering all target fields: confirmed/probable/suspected/unspecified case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, subnational locations, and dates reported.
search_reasoning: The upstream planned queries are a reasonable starting point but have two structural weaknesses: (1) they use rigid quoted phrases (e.g., "Salmonella outbreak United States 2024") that may suppress relevant results from CDC, FDA, and state health departments that use different phrasing; (2) the date-range string "2024-05-01-2024-07-31" embedded in query text is unlikely to match any real document and adds noise. For iteration 1, we prioritize the four highest-value query slots (max 4 per iteration) as follows: (a) a CDC-targeted web search for active outbreak investigations and multistate outbreak notices in the May–July 2024 window — the CDC's outbreak investigation pages and MMWR are the primary authoritative US source; (b) an FDA outbreak/recall-linked Salmonella search for the same window, since many US Salmonella outbreaks are food-vehicle linked and FDA issues advisories with case counts; (c) a broad web search for Salmonella multistate outbreaks and case counts in the US during summer 2024, without rigid quoting, to surface state health department advisories and ProMED/PAHO notices; (d) a news/situation-report search targeting specific outbreak events (e.g., linked to cucumbers, eggs, poultry, or other common vehicles) that were reported in May–July 2024, which will help identify subnational locations and hospitalization data. Literature queries are deferred to iteration 2 if needed, as peer-reviewed publications for mid-2024 events are unlikely to be indexed yet. The max-4-query constraint means we must prioritize breadth of authoritative source type over query-term variation.

query_batch.query: CDC Salmonella outbreak investigation 2024 cases hospitalizations deaths United States May June July
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC is the primary US federal authority for Salmonella surveillance. Its outbreak investigation pages and MMWR reports are the highest-trust source for confirmed case counts, hospitalization rates, deaths, and subnational location breakdowns. Targeting CDC directly without rigid quoting maximizes recall of relevant pages published in or covering May–July 2024.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC outbreak investigation pages, MMWR reports, CDC FoodNet surveillance summaries
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain, MMWR publication, official outbreak investigation notice

query_batch.query: FDA Salmonella outbreak recall advisory 2024 cases United States May June July food vehicle
query_batch.query_rationale: FDA issues outbreak advisories and recall notices for food-vehicle-linked Salmonella outbreaks, often including case counts, affected states, and hospitalization data. Many US Salmonella outbreaks in summer months are linked to produce, eggs, or poultry. FDA advisories frequently cross-reference CDC investigation data and provide subnational location detail.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: FDA outbreak advisory pages, FDA food safety alerts, FDA recall notices with epidemiological data
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: fda.gov domain, official outbreak advisory or recall notice with case count data

query_batch.query: Salmonella multistate outbreak United States 2024 cases deaths hospitalizations state health department
query_batch.query_rationale: A broad web search without rigid quoting will surface state health department advisories, ProMED posts, PAHO event notices, and aggregator pages (e.g., Outbreak News Today) that report Salmonella multistate outbreaks in the US during 2024. This captures subnational location data and corroborating case counts that may not appear in CDC/FDA pages alone. Avoiding exact-phrase quoting improves recall across varied agency naming conventions.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: State health department press releases, ProMED posts, PAHO event notices, public health news aggregators
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: State .gov domains, ProMED archive, PAHO PAHO.int, named public health official quotes with case counts

query_batch.query: Salmonella outbreak US 2024 sick hospitalized recalled food cucumbers eggs poultry May July cases
query_batch.query_rationale: News sources often report Salmonella outbreaks with specific case counts, hospitalization numbers, deaths, and subnational locations before official agency pages are updated. Including common food vehicles (cucumbers, eggs, poultry) known to drive summer US Salmonella outbreaks increases the chance of surfacing specific outbreak events within the May–July 2024 window. News reports also frequently cite official sources, enabling source triangulation.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: News articles from major outlets (Reuters, AP, NPR, local news) citing CDC/FDA/state health department data; Outbreak News Today; Food Safety News
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Named official source cited (CDC, FDA, state health dept), specific case/death/hospitalization numbers, dateline within May–July 2024

expected_evidence: CDC outbreak investigation page with case count, hospitalization count, death count, and affected states for a Salmonella outbreak active or reported in May–July 2024
MMWR report or CDC FoodNet summary with confirmed Salmonella case counts by state and date for 2024
FDA outbreak advisory or food safety alert with Salmonella case counts and subnational location data for May–July 2024

Originates from or cites a US federal agency (CDC, FDA, USDA) or state/territorial health department

language_or_localization_reasoning: All queries are in English. The United States is an English-language jurisdiction with all primary public health reporting in English. CDC, FDA, and state health departments publish exclusively in English for national surveillance data. No localization or translation is required for this task.
trust_considerations: Prefer cdc.gov and fda.gov pages as primary authoritative sources; treat as highest trust
State health department .gov pages are high trust for subnational data
ProMED and PAHO are high trust for international/aggregated situation reports
Food Safety News and Outbreak News Today are reputable secondary sources that consistently cite official data
News articles should only be used if they cite a named official source with specific quantitative data
Avoid sources that do not provide a date of publication or data currency indicator
Be alert to the distinction between outbreak investigation updates (which revise case counts over time) and final reports — prefer the most recent update within or just after the target window
stop_condition_hypothesis: Iteration 1 is sufficient if results yield: at least one CDC outbreak investigation page or MMWR report with case counts and dates in the target window; at least one FDA advisory or state health department report with subnational location data; and at least one news or situation report corroborating case/death/hospitalization figures. If these are absent or sparse, iteration 2 should target specific outbreak vehicles or state-level sources identified from iteration 1 metadata.

The date-range string '2024-05-01-2024-07-31' embedded in upstream query text is not a natural language pattern and is unlikely to match real documents — removed from iteration 1 queries

Salmonella outbreaks in the US are often reported with a lag; some May–July 2024 outbreaks may only appear in CDC pages updated in August–September 2024 — results should not be excluded solely because the page update date falls slightly outside the target window if the case dates are within scope

Multiple concurrent Salmonella outbreaks may be active in the same window (different serotypes, different food vehicles) — evidence collection should distinguish between outbreak events rather than aggregating all cases

Max 4 queries per iteration constraint means structured database and literature channels are not covered in iteration 1 — these should be prioritized in iteration 2 if official and news sources are insufficient

search_reasoning: Iteration 1 surfaced strong leads — particularly the FDA/CDC cucumber outbreak (June 2024, 449 cases, 31 states) and the Milo's Poultry Farms eggs outbreak (illnesses starting May 23, 2024) — but several critical gaps remain. First, the CDC cucumber outbreak index page (africana-06-24) returned only a brief snippet without full case/death/hospitalization counts; the full investigation update with final figures needs to be targeted. Second, the eggs outbreak page covers illnesses starting May 23, 2024, squarely within the target window, but the snippet only shows September/October 2024 update counts — an earlier update covering May–July 2024 specifically is needed. Third, the backyard poultry outbreak (513 sick, 134 hospitalized, 1 death) surfaced via an X/CDC tweet but lacks a date anchor — this may be a 2024 or 2025 event and needs a direct CDC investigation page. Fourth, the FSIS.usda.gov results (2 domains) were not summarized — USDA/FSIS may have issued recall/outbreak notices for poultry or meat-linked Salmonella in the target window. Fifth, no state-level subnational data (beyond state counts) has been confirmed, and the doh.wa.gov result was not summarized. Iteration 2 must close these gaps within the 4-query limit before the max-2-iteration bound is reached.
